paper.title: Lower Bounds on Regret for Noisy Gaussian Process Bandit Optimization

settings.name_in_paper: Simple regret, non-Bayesian GP bandit optimization, SE kernel
unmapped: f lies in the RKHS of the isotropic squared-exponential kernel with ||f||_k <= B (B may be known to the learner)
domain D=[0,1]^d; d and lengthscale l are Theta(1)
settings.definition_quote: We consider the optimization of a function $f$ defined on a compact domain $D = [0,1]^d$. ... we assume that the corresponding RKHS norm is bounded as $\|f\|_{k} \le B$. ... a noisy sample $y_t = f(x_t) + z_t$ is observed, with $z_t \sim N(0,\sigma^2)$ ... Simple regret: At the end of $T$ rounds, an additional point $x^{(T)}$ is reported, and the simple regret incurred is $r^{(T)} = f(x^*) - f(x^{(T)})$.

settings.definition_quote: We consider the optimization of a function $f$ defined on a compact domain $D = [0,1]^d$. ... $\|f\|_{k} \le B$ ... $z_t \sim N(0,\sigma^2)$ ... Simple regret ... $r^{(T)} = f(x^*) - f(x^{(T)})$.

symbols.B_rkhs: upper bound on the RKHS norm of f

conditions: algorithm achieves E[r^(T)] <= epsilon for every f in F_k(B)

source.label: thm:instantaneous
source.quote: Fix $\epsilon \in \big(0,\frac{1}{2}\big)$, $B > 0$, and $T \in \ZZ$. Suppose there exists an algorithm that, for any $f \in \Fc_k(B)$, achieves an average simple regret $\EE[r^{(T)}] \le \epsilon$ after $T$ rounds. Then, provided that $\frac{\epsilon}{B}$ is sufficiently small ... For $k = \kSE$, it is necessary that $T = \Omega\bigg( \frac{\sigma^2}{\epsilon^2} \Big(\log\frac{B}{\epsilon}\Big)^{d/2} \bigg)$.

results.notes: Lower bound on the number of rounds needed for expected simple regret epsilon. Section 5.4 argues the same scaling holds for a constant-probability version.

symbols.B_rkhs: upper bound on the RKHS norm of f

conditions: algorithm achieves E[r^(T)] <= epsilon for every f in F_k(B)
results.notes: Same theorem as r1, Matérn case.

bound.regime: sigma/B = O(sqrt(T)) with sufficiently small implied constant

symbols.B_rkhs: upper bound on the RKHS norm of f

conditions: sigma/B = O(sqrt(T)) with a sufficiently small implied constant

source.label: thm:cumulative
source.quote: Fix $B > 0$ and $T \in \ZZ$. Suppose there exists an algorithm that, for any $f \in \Fc_k(B)$, achieves an average cumulative regret of $\EE[R_T]$ after $T$ rounds. Then ... For $k = \kSE$, it is necessary that $\EE[R_T] = \Omega\Bigg( \sqrt{T\sigma^2 \Big(\log \frac{B^2 T}{\sigma^2} \Big)^{d/2} } \Bigg)$ provided that $\frac{\sigma}{B} = O\big(\sqrt{T}\big)$ with a sufficiently small implied constant.

results.notes: Regret is defined through the function values (means), so it is recorded as pseudo-regret. Worst case over f in the RKHS ball.
